standalone_working_capital_answer.pipeline: Writer 3.5 and reviewer 1.1 with 4096 reviewer token allowance; generation scope says automated review can miss errors.

supported_points: Required incremental working capital belongs in deduction (c) when needed to maintain competitive position and unit volume.
Usual LIFO qualification remains conditional on unchanged volume and is not turned into a blanket inventory exemption.
1998 Buffett net-cash versus gross-cash and fixed-asset maintenance comments are substantially preserved.

issues.claim: When (c) exceeds reported depreciation (component b), GAAP earnings overstate owner earnings.
issues.source: 1986 u286 defines b; u290 states c>b condition.
issues.finding: Component (b) includes depreciation, depletion, amortization and certain other noncash charges. Replacing the complete addback with depreciation alone changes the condition for GAAP earnings exceeding owner earnings. The correct fuller definition in the opening does not make the later explicit component label accurate.

issues.claim: Buffett noted this overstatement was common in oil and manufacturing, retailing, extractive companies and utilities generally.
issues.finding: u290 describes the broader likelihood and supplies oil as a conspicuous historical example. u292 says maintenance component(c) is significant in the named categories, not that it exceeds the complete addback(b) in each of them. The draft merges different predicates into a stronger attributed sector claim.

standalone_working_capital_answer.question: How does required working capital affect owner earnings?
standalone_working_capital_answer.semantic_assessment: Not independently approved as received. Correct core formula and qualification are followed by unsupported practical expansions. The separate automatic source check approved this draft and did not prevent the issues.
standalone_working_capital_answer.source_review: Cited 1986 u286 and u287 checked against canonical text; cited 1998 chapter 8 p007 and p009 checked with full chapter context and retained attribution metadata.
improvements: Full component(b) retains depreciation, depletion, amortization and certain other noncash charges.
The previous c>depreciation shortcut and manufacturing/retail/extractive/utility sector conflation are absent.

Opening and complete formula paragraph accurately explain additional working capital required to maintain competitive position and unit volume, and retain the usual LIFO/unchanged-volume qualification.

issues.claim: For non-LIFO businesses with growing unit volumes or rising input costs, the working-capital drain reduces owner earnings; evaluators must deduct permanent additional working capital pulled in by unit-volume growth or inflation.
issues.finding: u286 specifies additional working capital needed to maintain competitive position and unit volume. It does not establish the added non-LIFO/input-cost mechanism or the broader mandatory growth/inflation test. The practical paragraph expands the stated maintenance condition into a different deduction rule and gives source-attributed guidance beyond the supplied text.

issues.claim: A business requiring more and more reinvestment just to maintain its position produces less cash for owners over time.
issues.finding: The passages contrast businesses requiring little capital with forced growth at very low reinvestment returns. They do not establish an unconditional time-series decline in cash available to owners without considering changing earnings or reinvestment returns.

issues.claim: Buffett has also stated the best-business/worst-business comparisons from P12-007 and P12-009.
issues.finding: Both supplied canonical speaker fields are null with preceding-label attribution explicitly pending review. The prompt forbids resolving a null speaker from familiar wording. The draft states Buffett confidently. This is loss of the packet uncertainty, not proof that the historical speaker was someone else.

standalone_working_capital_answer.quality_note: The answer also substantially exceeds the new 100–160-word narrow-answer target and repeats the formula; this is an instruction/usability miss, distinct from the material source-support issues.
